A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SNG/SVS/SPRING analysis. Their main texts, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical experiments on synthetic linear least-quadratics, including proxy comparisons, spectral-decay effects, convergence-parameter estimates, and SPRING acceleration.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds a neural-network experiment solving a discrete Poisson problem, with results summarized across five runs.

M1.justification: The SNG update, squared volume sampling distribution, and SPRING iteration remain unchanged. The periodic ResNet introduced in v3 is an ansatz for the added evaluation, without changing the optimization algorithms.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates synthetic linear least-quadratics problems. v3 retains this coverage and adds a periodic discrete Poisson problem with a nonlinear neural-network ansatz, substantially extending evaluation into the scientific machine learning setting motivating the paper.

E2.justification: Matched proxy experiments retain the two-independent-batch proxy, SVS-SNG, and uniform single-batch SNG. The added Poisson experiment uses this same comparator set. Figure 5 retains the SNG-versus-SPRING comparison.

E3.justification: The added Poisson protocol uses m=100, n=7801, k=10, and 1000 iterations, with regularization and step-size sweeps fixing the other parameter at 0.01. Appendix J.1 specifies zero-mean adjustment before computing L2 errors. Matched LLQ protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 2 extends sensitivity analysis of proxy fidelity and stability across regularization and step size to the nonlinear Poisson setting. The inflated-row robustness experiment survives as Figure 7, and the spectral-decay and sample-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 2 newly reports five-run means with shaded minimum-to-maximum ranges. v2 has no comparable optimizer-run uncertainty reporting. The existing Figure 3 Monte Carlo estimation budget and sample counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds Poisson error curves showing SVS-SNG closely tracking uniform single-batch SNG while the two-batch proxy behaves differently. All original numerical plots are retained: v2 Figures 2 and 6 become v3 Figures 6 and 7, and Figures 3–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Theorem G.1 and its proof extend the rate analysis to linear ansatzes with smooth, strongly convex losses and possible inconsistency, including a residual-error floor. Proposition 5.3 adds the orthonormal-row case and regularized endpoint bounds, and changes the uniform-sampling bound from 1 + max_i ||J_i||^2/lambda to 1 + k max_i ||J_i||^2/lambda. Additional proof constants are corrected. The strong-compatibility result is retained as Proposition F.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions retain their meaning. Contribution 2 additionally claims the explicit extension to smooth, strongly convex and possibly inconsistent problems, modestly broadening the stated theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the SGD comparison to linear convergence rates in standard smooth, strongly convex settings. It replaces v2's asserted local nonlinear extension with future-work language, explains the inconsistency error floor, and develops more concrete possibilities for approximate SVS sampling.

D1.justification: Appendix J replaces v2's supplementary-code notice with an explicit repository link. New Appendix J.1 specifies the Poisson discretization, target solution, five-layer width-50 periodic ResNet, initialization, automatic differentiation, and local gradient computation. Existing LLQ implementation and tuning details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on practical DPP sampling, sketched Newton methods, SGD convergence, stochastic dual ascent, and ResNets. These support localized expansions of background and interpretation; the central positioning relative to stochastic preconditioning and sketch-and-project methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v3 moves and expands the two-batch explanation into Appendix A, adds the spectral-rate discussion in Appendix B, relocates strong compatibility to Appendix F, improves proof exposition, and adds an impact statement.

P2.justification: v3 adds a two-panel Poisson figure with uncertainty shading and an expanded caption. The original Figure 2 moves to the appendix as Figure 6, and the original Figure 6 becomes Figure 7. The other figures retain their displays, with limited accompanying page reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens rigor through the explicit inconsistency extension and mathematical corrections, and improves empirical relevance through the five-run neural Poisson experiment. Added implementation details and a concrete code-access reference improve reproducibility information. These are bounded gains to an already developed central analysis: the uniform-sampling gamma bound becomes looser, and the extended rate theorem still requires a linear ansatz and SVS.
